get.summary: Start GitHub sign-in or account linking
get.description: Browser navigation, not an `Api` call: the official client opens `API_URL + 'auth/github?'` in a popup window. When signed in it appends `token=<current auth token>` (linking GitHub to the signed-in account); with `repoScope=1` it requests repository access (used by the GitHub code-sync settings after `GET /api/auth/github/check-repo-scope` answered `no scope`). On completion the popup posts a JSON string message to the opener; the client parses it, reads `token` (stored as the new session token), `email`, and `username` (absent for a newly registered account, which the client then sends to `/register`).

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: Current auth token, appended only when the user is already signed in (links GitHub to that account).

parameters.name: repoScope
parameters.description: `1` to request GitHub repository scope; omitted otherwise.

default.description: Browser navigation opened in a popup window; the response (OAuth redirect chain and the final page) is not read as JSON by the official client.

get.x-unverified: The HTTP responses of the navigation (redirect to GitHub, callback URL, final HTML page) and the exact postMessage payload beyond `token`/`email`/`username` are not evidenced; the popup message is a browser `postMessage`, not part of the HTTP response body.

post.summary: Reset a password with a recovery token
post.description: Completes e-mail password recovery. The recovery page (`/register/recover?t=<token>`) first posts only `{token}` to validate the link: the logical error `invalid password` means the token is valid (the form is shown), any other error marks the link invalid. Submitting the form posts `{token, password}`; success shows a confirmation, any error a generic failure. The official client only submits passwords that consist of letters, digits and `!@#$%^&*(),./\[]{}'";=+|_-?~`:<>` characters and contain at least one digit and one non-digit.
